(1) habit moderates the relationship between intention and continued IS usage and (2) satisfaction, frequency of use, and comprehensiness of use are key to habit development in the context of information systems usage.
habit moderates the effect of intentions on IS continuance behavior and that habit is driven by the frequency of IS usage, satisfaction with IS usage, and the comprehensiveness of IS usage.
habit acts as moderator of the relationship between behavioral intentions and continued IS usage and that satisfaction, frequency, and comprehensibility of usage are important drivers of habit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how habit affects the predictive power of intention in the context of continuous IS usage behavior.
how the role of intention is limited in the context of habitual behaviors, and how the habit construct can be incorporated in the context of information systems continuance research.

the habit construct has the potential to significantly enhance the predictive power of the theory of continued IS usage, and that the proposed framework provides a solid basis for future research in the area.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
while intention may be an important predictor of initial IS usage, it may not be the most important predictor of continued IS usage behavior.
habit is an important determinant of continued IS usage and that its role is to moderate the effect of intention.
habit is an important construct that should be considered in IS research and in particular, in the context of the continued use of IS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IS researchers need to be aware of the role of habit in IS continuance behavior and the implications this may have for the explanatory power of intention.
